source_meta._title: Players are disconnected from servers when opening command blocks that consist of large numbers of characters within the previous output field

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition using a vanilla dedicated multiplayer server, not a singleplayer world or integrated LAN server. Run both the dedicated server and test client on 1.18.2. Use one operator test player in Creative mode, with command blocks enabled on the server. Keep the test player close to the generated command block and ensure no other player is closer to it.
preconditions: A vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.18.2 dedicated-server directory has been initialized, the EULA has been accepted, and server.properties has been generated.
The server is stopped before editing server.properties.
The server and connecting client use exactly the same Minecraft version.
The test account's exact Java Edition username and the server address are known.
The test account can be made a server operator.

Only the test player should be online during reproduction. If additional players must be present, they must remain farther from the repeating command block than the test player because the block's command targets @p.

Use an ordinary test world in which the test player can stand in a loaded, open area with replaceable space three blocks away in the positive Z direction. No particular seed or coordinates are supplied by the report.
Do not perform this reproduction in singleplayer; the report explicitly states that the issue does not occur there.

steps.action: With the dedicated server stopped, open server.properties in a text editor. Find enable-command-block and set it to true. Save the file without changing the property name.
steps.success_cue: server.properties is saved and contains exactly one active enable-command-block=true line.

steps.action: In server.properties, ensure the operator permission level is at least 2 so an operator can use and open command blocks. For a deterministic configuration, set it to 2, then save the file.
steps.success_cue: server.properties is saved with op-permission-level=2 and enable-command-block=true.

steps.action: Start the vanilla dedicated server using the 1.18.2 server installation. Do not connect until startup is complete.
steps.success_cue: The server console displays its normal startup-complete message containing "Done", and the console accepts input.

steps.action: In the dedicated-server console, grant operator status to the test account. Enter the console command without a leading slash, replacing <test-player-username> with the account's exact username.
steps.success_cue: The server console confirms that the named test account was made a server operator, or otherwise confirms that it is already an operator.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition 1.18.2 on the test client. Select Multiplayer, connect to the prepared dedicated server, and wait for the world to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The test player is present on the dedicated server, surrounding terrain has rendered, and movement and chat input respond normally.

steps.action: Put the operator test player into Creative mode, which is required to open a command block interface on a multiplayer server. Press T to open chat, type the command exactly with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is in Creative mode, indicated by unrestricted flight being available after double-tapping Space and by the absence of the normal Survival health and hunger interface.

steps.action: Move the test player to a loaded, open area. Make sure the space at the player's current X and Y coordinates and three blocks in the positive Z direction is available for a command block. Remain in this area for the rest of the reproduction.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a responsive, fully loaded area with room for a block to appear three blocks away horizontally.

steps.action: Unlock every recipe for the test player. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the report's command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without a red command error, and chat reports that recipes were granted to the test player.

steps.action: Confirm that the test player is the only online player, or at minimum is the player nearest to the location three blocks in the positive Z direction. Do not move far away after this point because the repeating command block will use @p to select the nearest player.
steps.success_cue: The test player remains within a few blocks of the intended command-block location, with no other player closer to that location.

steps.action: Create the active repeating command block using the exact command from the report. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command exactly with the leading slash and unchanged NBT syntax, and press Enter. The relative coordinates place it at the player's current X and Y coordinates and Z plus 3.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without a red syntax error, and a purple repeating command block is visible approximately three blocks from the player.

steps.action: Do not open the command block yet. Keep the test player near it and wait two seconds so the Always Active repeating command block can execute multiple server ticks and write the result of data get entity @p into its previous-output data.
steps.success_cue: At least two seconds have elapsed, the command block remains loaded near the player, and normal movement still responds.

steps.action: Face the purple repeating command block and position the center crosshair directly over one of its visible faces while remaining within interaction range.
steps.success_cue: The repeating command block is under the crosshair and close enough to use without moving.

steps.action: Use the targeted repeating command block exactly once by pressing the Use Item/Place Block control, which is right-click by default. Do not repeatedly click, issue another command, or intentionally trigger the setup again.
steps.success_cue: A single Use Block input has just been sent to the repeating command block; immediately hand control to the observation subsystem without evaluating the result.

stor.handoff_condition: The operator test player has unlocked all recipes, remained nearest to an active repeating command block running data get entity @p, waited for the block to populate its previous output, and has just right-clicked that command block once on the dedicated server. Begin observation immediately.
uncertainties: The authored Steps to Reproduce explicitly name 22w16b, while the issue's affected-version list begins with 1.18.2. Following the required affected-version selection rule, this plan recommends 1.18.2. The identical report commands can be rerun on 22w16b if strict fidelity to the originally documented server instance is required.

The report supplies no world seed, coordinates, world type, server address, or test-player username. The plan therefore uses any loaded open area and placeholders for deployment-specific connection information.

The report does not specify how long the repeating command block must execute before it is opened. A two-second delay is a practical inference intended to ensure that at least one command execution has completed without introducing excessive repetition.
Creative mode and operator permission are not stated in the formal report steps, but they are operational prerequisites for opening a command block interface on a Java Edition multiplayer server.

source_meta._title: io.netty.handler.codec.EncoderException when evaluating too many entity selectors in chat preview

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition dedicated server and one matching Java Edition client, both running 1.19 Pre-release 1 (launcher version ID 1.19-pre1). Run the server with Java 17 in a new, isolated server directory, use its ordinary newly generated Overworld, and keep the dedicated-server console visible for the observation agent. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_1.19_Pre-release_1))
preconditions: Use exactly Minecraft: Java Edition 1.19 Pre-release 1 for both the dedicated server and client; do not use the fixed version, 1.19 Pre-release 2.
Use a vanilla dedicated server rather than single-player. Do not install plugins, mods, datapacks, or proxy software that could replace command parsing or chat preview handling.

The client must be able to connect to the dedicated server. If both run on the same computer, the client can use localhost; otherwise, use the server's reachable address and configure networking as needed.

The server must have chat preview enabled with previews-chat=true in server.properties. Chat preview was available for /say in this affected version. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_1.19?utm_source=openai))

The reproducing player must have operator permission so that /say and its entity selectors can be parsed as a usable command. Grant operator status from the dedicated-server console after the player joins. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Commands/op))
Keep the client connection view and dedicated-server console available for immediate handoff to the separate observation subsystem.
Do not press Enter to send the reproduction command. The trigger is evaluation of the unsent command by chat preview while its text is being prepared.

steps.action: Create a new empty directory dedicated to this reproduction. Obtain the vanilla dedicated-server JAR for Minecraft Java Edition 1.19 Pre-release 1, place it in that directory, and rename it to server.jar for the commands below. This version is identified as 1.19-pre1 by the launcher and requires Java 17. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_1.19_Pre-release_1))
steps.success_cue: The isolated directory contains the 1.19 Pre-release 1 server file named server.jar.

steps.action: Open a terminal or command prompt in the server directory and perform the server's initial launch. Do not enter this command in Minecraft chat.
steps.success_cue: The server creates its initial configuration files, including eula.txt, and reports that the EULA must be accepted before normal startup.

steps.action: After the initial server process has stopped, open eula.txt in a plain-text editor and change its EULA setting to true. Save the file without changing its filename.
steps.success_cue: The saved eula.txt file contains eula=true.

steps.action: Open server.properties in a plain-text editor. Find the previews-chat property and set it to true. If the property is absent, add the exact line as a new property. Save the file. Chat preview for commands such as /say is part of the affected version's behavior. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_1.19?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The saved server.properties file contains exactly one active previews-chat=true setting.

steps.action: Start the dedicated server again from its directory. Leave this terminal open throughout reproduction so the observation agent can inspect server output.
steps.success_cue: The console reports that server startup is complete and presents a usable server-console input prompt; the ordinary server world has been generated or loaded.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for 1.19-pre1, use a separate game directory if available, and launch it. On the main menu, confirm the displayed client version is 1.19 Pre-release 1 rather than 1.19 Pre-release 2 or a release version. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_1.19_Pre-release_1))
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft client is at the main menu and identifies itself as 1.19 Pre-release 1.

steps.action: Before joining, navigate from the main menu to Options, then Chat Settings. Set the Chat Preview option to ON if it is disabled, then return to the main menu. This client option existed because chat preview could be globally disabled by the client. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_1.19?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The client-side Chat Preview setting is ON.

steps.action: Select Multiplayer, use Direct Connection or add the server, enter its address, and join. Use localhost when the client and server are running on the same computer; otherwise use the actual server address. Acknowledge or continue past any chat-preview warning shown while connecting.
steps.success_cue: The player is present in the dedicated server's generated Overworld, surrounding terrain has rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: In the dedicated-server console, grant operator status to the connected player. Replace <player_name> with the player's exact Java account name. Because this is the server console, enter the command without a leading slash. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Commands/op))
steps.success_cue: The server console confirms that the named player was made a server operator, or otherwise confirms that the player is already an operator.

steps.action: Return focus to the connected client. Wait until the nearby chunks are fully rendered and player controls respond normally. Remain in the ordinary Overworld and do not remove naturally loaded entities.
steps.success_cue: The player remains connected in the normal generated world, terrain is loaded, and the server console remains accessible for monitoring.

steps.action: Verify that command chat preview is active before using the oversized selector input. Press T, type the harmless unsent test command exactly as shown, and do not press Enter. Wait for the preview area above the chat input to respond.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted as valid input and a server-controlled preview is shown or updated above the chat edit box.

steps.action: Clear the harmless test without sending it. With the chat field focused, press Ctrl+A to select all text and then press Backspace. Keep the chat screen open.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is empty, chat remains open, and no command has been sent.

steps.action: Prepare the high-selector command in the operating-system clipboard so it can be inserted in one input action. Generate exactly the four characters /say followed by exactly 80 repetitions of a space and @e. The resulting text must be 244 characters long, contain 80 @e selectors, have one space before every selector, and contain no line break.
steps.success_cue: The clipboard contains a single 244-character line beginning with /say @e and containing exactly 80 occurrences of @e.

steps.action: With the empty chat field still focused, press Ctrl+V once to paste the complete 244-character command. Do not press Enter, do not close chat, and do not interact with any screen that appears after the paste. Pasting is used to make the large selector-bearing text change a single deterministic chat-preview request.
steps.exact_input: "/say" + (" @e" repeated exactly 80 times); paste with Ctrl+V and do not press Enter
steps.success_cue: The paste action has been issued while chat preview is enabled; no command-send action has been performed.

stor.handoff_condition: The 244-character unsent /say command containing 80 @e selectors has just been inserted into the chat input while server and client chat preview are enabled. Enter has not been pressed, the client must receive no further input, and the dedicated-server console remains visible. Begin observing the client connection state and server output immediately.
uncertainties: The report does not specify an exact selector count at which the oversized preview occurs. It gives ten selectors as an example and states that continuing to add @e eventually reaches the trigger. The plan uses 80 selectors as a deterministic high-count input while retaining the reported /say and @e syntax.

The amount of preview data generated by each @e depends on the entities currently loaded in the ordinary server world. The report provides no seed, coordinates, entity count, or explicit entity-spawning setup, so the plan preserves its stated normal-world condition rather than inventing a custom population.

Pasting the full selector sequence in one action is a practical execution choice intended to produce one clearly bounded trigger and immediate observation handoff. The report describes continuing to type @e but does not explicitly discuss clipboard input.

The report does not specify an operating system, server memory allocation, world seed, game mode, coordinates, or a requirement for multiple players. The plan therefore uses one operator player, the server's default world settings, and no special seed or coordinates.

The external sources were used only to verify version-sensitive operational details: the launcher identifier 1.19-pre1, Java 17, the previews-chat server property, command chat preview availability, the client Chat Preview option, and dedicated-server operator handling.

source_meta._title: External inventory changes except for the hotbar are not registered in a creative mode item selection screen

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.20.4 in a new single-player Creative-mode world using the integrated server. Use the normal Creative inventory interface; no seed, coordinates, dedicated server, additional players, commands, or datapacks are required.
preconditions: Launch the first listed affected version, Java Edition 1.20.4; do not use the listed fix version 24w38a.
Use a newly created Creative-mode world so the player's 27-slot main inventory and nine-slot hotbar begin empty.
Perform the trigger while the Creative inventory remains open on a tab other than Survival Inventory; this plan uses the Search Items tab.

Use two different item types: Stone to occupy every hotbar slot and Red Wool as the item that will be dropped and picked up. The target item must not match the hotbar item, so it cannot merge into a hotbar stack.
Default mouse controls and the default E key for Open Inventory are assumed. If controls are rebound, use the corresponding Open Inventory, left-click, and pointer actions.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select and start a Java Edition installation for exactly version 1.20.4. Wait for the game to reach its main menu.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is open and the displayed game version is 1.20.4.

steps.action: Choose Singleplayer, create a new world, set Game Mode to Creative, and create the world. Do not reuse a world whose player inventory may already contain items.
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a new world in Creative mode, with an empty visible hotbar and Creative-mode capabilities such as unrestricted flight.

steps.action: Wait until the nearby terrain has rendered and player input responds normally. Stand still on solid ground and aim the view down at the block directly beneath or immediately in front of the player; this helps the subsequently dropped item remain within automatic pickup range.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on solid ground, nearby chunks are rendered, and the view is aimed almost straight down at nearby ground.

steps.action: Press E, the default Open Inventory key, to open the Creative inventory interface. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ABeginner%27s_guide?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The Creative item-selection screen is visible, including category tabs, the item catalog, and the nine hotbar slots along its bottom edge.

steps.action: For an initial-state check, select the tab whose hover tooltip reads “Survival Inventory.” Confirm that all 27 main-inventory slots and all nine hotbar slots are empty. If they are not empty, discard this world and repeat from step 2 with a new world rather than clearing items during the trigger sequence.
steps.success_cue: The Survival Inventory tab is selected and the player's main inventory and hotbar contain no items.

steps.action: Select the Creative tab whose hover tooltip reads “Search Items.” Click inside its search field and enter “stone.” Do not return to the Survival Inventory tab after this point.
steps.success_cue: The Search Items tab is active and the item results include the ordinary Stone block item.

steps.action: Fill only the hotbar with Stone. For hotbar slot 1, left-click the Stone result to take a stack onto the mouse cursor, then left-click hotbar slot 1 to place it. Repeat the same two-click cycle for hotbar slots 2 through 9. Inventory left-clicking picks up or places an entire stack. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ABeginner%27s_guide?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: left-click Stone; left-click hotbar slots 1 through 9, one slot at a time
steps.success_cue: Every one of the nine hotbar slots contains Stone, no hotbar slot is empty, and the mouse cursor is not carrying an item.

steps.action: While remaining on the Search Items tab, click the search field, select its existing contents, and replace them with “red wool.”
steps.success_cue: The Search Items tab remains active and the search results include the Red Wool item.

steps.action: Left-click the Red Wool result once to take a Red Wool stack onto the mouse cursor. Do not place it into any inventory or hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: A Red Wool stack is attached to the mouse cursor, while all nine hotbar slots remain occupied by Stone.

steps.action: Move the mouse pointer completely outside the rectangular Creative inventory panel and over the shaded world background, then left-click once. This drops the cursor-held stack into the world. Keep the Creative inventory open on the Search Items tab; do not press E, Escape, or select another tab. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki%3AProjects/Indonesian_translation/Persediaan?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The Red Wool stack is no longer attached to the cursor, all hotbar slots remain full of Stone, and the Search Items screen is still open.

steps.action: Without closing the Creative inventory or changing tabs, wait for the dropped Red Wool to pass its pickup delay and be collected automatically. Continue only when the item-pickup sound is heard; if visible around the edge of the interface, the dropped item entity should also disappear. Do not perform any inventory interaction after the pickup cue.
steps.success_cue: The Red Wool pickup event has just occurred while the Creative inventory is still open on Search Items and the hotbar is still full of Stone.

stor.handoff_condition: The externally dropped Red Wool has just been picked up while the player's nine hotbar slots remain filled with Stone and the Creative inventory remains open on the non-Survival Search Items tab. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately, before closing the screen, switching tabs, clicking slots, or otherwise forcing an inventory refresh.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a seed, coordinates, server type, hotbar filler item, or exact target item. A new single-player Creative world, Stone filler stacks, and Red Wool are deterministic practical choices; the report permits any items as long as the hotbar is full and the dropped item is a different type.

The report does not state the exact GUI action used to throw the item. This plan uses the standard inventory action of carrying an item on the cursor and left-clicking outside the inventory panel, which was externally verified.

Looking down before opening the inventory is not a reported requirement; it is a practical measure intended to keep the dropped item close enough to be picked up without closing the Creative inventory or moving the player.
The comment mentions reproduction in 1.21.1, but 1.21.1 is not included in the report's formal Affects versions field, so it was not added to affected_versions.
The attachment images were not required to execute the supplied textual reproduction and were not used.

source_meta._title: Entity interpolation for high speed projectiles is wildly inaccurate

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.7 in a single-player Creative-mode world with command permissions available. Use an open area with an unobstructed view of the sky. Vanilla entity hitboxes must be visible before the summon command is executed. No particular seed, coordinates, graphics setting, resource pack, mod, or dedicated server is specified by the report.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.7; do not use fix version 25w32a for this reproduction.
Use a world in which the player can execute commands. Creating a new Creative-mode single-player world is the simplest implementation because it provides command access and easy movement.
Ensure the player is in an open location where blocks, trees, cave ceilings, or structures do not obstruct the sky directly above the summon position.
Use the fourth command supplied by the report, because Comment 2 explicitly states that executing the fourth command while looking upward with hitboxes enabled is sufficient.
Be ready to begin observing immediately when the command is submitted, because the summoned arrow starts moving as soon as it is created.

steps.action: From the Minecraft Launcher, start a Java Edition installation configured for version 1.21.7. Wait at the title screen until the version identifier confirms that 1.21.7 is running.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition title screen is loaded and displays version 1.21.7.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set the game mode to Creative, and create the world. If using an existing world instead, ensure commands are permitted before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The player is fully loaded into a world and has Creative-mode command access.

steps.action: Wait for the nearby terrain to finish rendering. Confirm that looking around and moving responds normally before preparing the command.
steps.success_cue: Surrounding chunks are rendered and player controls respond without world-loading interruption.

steps.action: Position the player beneath an unobstructed section of sky. If necessary in Creative mode, double-tap the Jump control, which is Space by default, to begin flying and move away from trees, overhangs, cave ceilings, or structures. Stop in a stable position with clear vertical space above the player.
steps.exact_input: Space twice, if Creative flight is needed
steps.success_cue: Looking directly upward from the player's position shows open sky rather than a nearby block or structure.

steps.action: Enable Minecraft's entity hitbox display by pressing the debug hitbox shortcut. With default controls this is F3+B; on keyboards where function keys require a modifier, hold Fn as well. Release the keys after toggling the display on.
steps.success_cue: A debug confirmation indicates that hitboxes are shown; visible nearby entities, if any, have hitbox outlines.

steps.action: Aim the camera upward into the unobstructed sky, preferably nearly straight up. Keep the camera in this orientation so that the high-speed arrow's path begins within the visible part of the screen.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair points upward into open sky and no block is directly between the player and the sky.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat control, which is T by default. Do not turn the camera after opening chat.
steps.success_cue: The chat command input is open while the view remains aimed upward.

steps.action: Enter the fourth summon command from the report exactly as written, including the leading slash, capitalization, coordinates, NBT braces, decimal values, commas, and brackets. Do not submit it yet until observation can begin immediately.
steps.success_cue: The complete command `/summon minecraft:arrow ~ ~1 ~ {Motion:[1.0,10.0,0.0]}` is present in the chat input with no alterations.

steps.action: Press Enter once to execute the command. Keep looking upward and do not immediately move the player, turn the camera, disable hitboxes, pause, or open another interface.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without a red syntax or permission error, chat closes, and an arrow has been summoned one block above the player with the supplied motion while hitbox rendering remains enabled.

stor.handoff_condition: The command `/summon minecraft:arrow ~ ~1 ~ {Motion:[1.0,10.0,0.0]}` has just been executed once in Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.7 while the camera is aimed upward into open sky and entity hitboxes are enabled. The arrow is now in flight; hand off immediately to the observation subsystem without changing the camera or debug-display state.
uncertainties: The description lists four arrow summon commands, but Comment 2 states that the fourth command alone is sufficient while looking upward with hitboxes enabled. This plan therefore uses only the fourth command as the shortest deterministic trigger.

Single-player Creative mode and the use of an open-sky test location are practical execution choices. The report requires command execution and an upward view but does not mandate a particular game mode, seed, coordinate, or world type.

The report does not explain how the attachment's colored green and white visualization was produced. This plan uses Minecraft's standard F3+B hitbox display because Comment 2 explicitly confirms that hitboxes are sufficient, and it does not attempt to recreate any unspecified attachment-only overlay.

The formal Affects Versions field lists only 1.21.7. Although a later comment claims the problem also remains in 1.21.8, 1.21.8 is not added to affected_versions because it is not present in the report's formal affected-version list.

source_meta._title: Client continues to connect to server after canceling on 'Connecting to server' screen

stor.environment: Use an unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.8 client in a fresh game session. Provide two distinct, simultaneously reachable multiplayer server endpoints, Server A and Server B, which both accept connections from the same 1.8 test account. Prefer controlled vanilla-compatible test servers rather than public servers. Server A's connection establishment must be slow enough that the client remains on the 'Connecting to server' screen long enough to press its Cancel button; the report suggests inducing this with delayed DNS/IP lookup through a proxy. Server B should connect normally. Do not use the listed fix version, 1.20 Pre-release 5.
preconditions: A valid Minecraft account is available and can use multiplayer in Minecraft Java Edition 1.8.
Two different server addresses are available: <SERVER_A_ADDRESS> and <SERVER_B_ADDRESS>. They must lead to separate servers, not aliases for the same server.
Both servers are running, accept the Minecraft 1.8 client protocol, and permit the same test account to join.
The executor is authorized to test against both servers. Controlled test servers are strongly preferred because the report describes connection-state and item-transfer side effects.

Server A is configured, directly or through a test proxy/DNS mechanism, so connection establishment remains incomplete long enough for the client to display and accept the Cancel button. Server B is not subject to that delay.
The Minecraft client has been completely closed before beginning, so no connection left over from an earlier test can affect this reproduction.
The affected version selected in the launcher is exactly Minecraft 1.8, the first entry in the report's affected-version list.

steps.action: Start or verify both multiplayer servers. Wait until each server has completed startup and is ready to accept connections. Use the server consoles or another out-of-band readiness check; do not join either server from the test client yet.
steps.success_cue: Server A and Server B are both online under different addresses and are ready to accept the Minecraft 1.8 test account.

steps.action: Apply a connection-establishment delay to Server A. Use the test environment's proxy or DNS controls to delay Server A's DNS lookup or connection sufficiently for the Minecraft client to remain on the connection screen. Do not delay Server B. The report does not prescribe a specific proxy product or configuration.
steps.success_cue: Server A remains reachable but is expected to leave enough time to click Cancel before world loading completes; Server B remains normally reachable.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation/profile for exactly Minecraft 1.8 and start the game. Do not select 1.20 Pre-release 5, which is listed as a fix version.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.8 main menu is displayed in a newly started client session.

steps.action: From the main menu, left-click Multiplayer.
steps.success_cue: The Play Multiplayer server-list screen is open.

steps.action: If Server A is not already present, left-click Add server, enter a recognizable name such as Server A and enter <SERVER_A_ADDRESS> in the Server Address field, then left-click Done. If it is already present with the correct address, leave it unchanged.
steps.exact_input: Server Name: Server A; Server Address: <SERVER_A_ADDRESS>
steps.success_cue: A server-list entry labeled Server A is visible and points to <SERVER_A_ADDRESS>.

steps.action: If Server B is not already present, left-click Add server, enter a recognizable name such as Server B and enter <SERVER_B_ADDRESS> in the Server Address field, then left-click Done. If it is already present with the correct address, leave it unchanged.
steps.exact_input: Server Name: Server B; Server Address: <SERVER_B_ADDRESS>
steps.success_cue: Separate Server A and Server B entries are visible in the multiplayer server list.

steps.action: Select the Server A entry and begin connecting by left-clicking Join Server. Double-clicking the Server A entry is also acceptable, but issue only one join action.
steps.exact_input: Select Server A; left-click Join Server
steps.success_cue: The server list is replaced by a connection-progress screen for Server A.

steps.action: Wait only until the connection-progress screen displays 'Connecting to server' and presents an enabled Cancel button. Do not wait for Server A's terrain, HUD, or in-world play screen to appear.
steps.success_cue: The client is still connecting to Server A, the in-world play screen has not loaded, and the Cancel button is available.

steps.action: While the client is still on the Server A connection-progress screen, immediately left-click Cancel once. Do not allow Server A to finish loading before this input.
steps.success_cue: The connection-progress screen closes and the client returns to either the multiplayer server list or the main menu.

steps.action: Proceed back to the multiplayer server list without intentionally waiting. If cancellation returned directly to the server list, perform no navigation action. If it returned to the main menu, immediately left-click Multiplayer.
steps.exact_input: Multiplayer, only if the main menu is displayed
steps.success_cue: The multiplayer server list containing Server A and Server B is displayed again, with no client restart or deliberate delay since Cancel was pressed.

steps.action: As soon as the server list is usable, select Server B and begin connecting by left-clicking Join Server. Do not reconnect to Server A, restart the client, or enter another world between the cancellation and this action.
steps.exact_input: Select Server B; left-click Join Server
steps.success_cue: The server list is replaced by the connection-progress screen for Server B.

steps.action: Allow the Server B connection to complete. Wait until the client transitions to an in-world play screen and enough initial terrain has rendered to identify that Server B was entered. Do not disconnect, return to the menu, or restart the game after reaching this state.
steps.success_cue: An in-world play screen reached through Server B is displayed after the canceled Server A attempt, and the client session remains open for immediate observation.

stor.handoff_condition: The client has just completed entry into Server B in the same uninterrupted Minecraft 1.8 session in which Server A was canceled at the 'Connecting to server' screen. The in-world play screen is visible. Do not disconnect, reconnect, change worlds, or restart the client; hand control to the observation subsystem now.
uncertainties: The report does not provide the addresses or configurations of the two original servers. <SERVER_A_ADDRESS> and <SERVER_B_ADDRESS> must be supplied by the test environment.

The reproduction is timing-sensitive. The report does not state an exact maximum interval between pressing Cancel and starting the Server B connection; perform the second connection as soon as the interface permits and introduce no intentional pause.
The report suggests increasing Server A's DNS/IP lookup time with a proxy that forces DNS lookups, but it does not name a proxy product or provide exact proxy configuration commands.

The original description used CubeKrowd as Server A and an unnamed second server. This plan substitutes authorized controlled servers because later report comments state that the issue was confirmed on vanilla and could be reproduced with other servers.

A separate F5/ESC reproduction variant in the comments was specifically documented for Minecraft 1.8.7. It is not used here because the required recommended version is Minecraft 1.8, the first affected version listed in the report.

If Server A connects too quickly for the Cancel input to occur before world loading, that attempt does not satisfy the report's timing precondition. Increase the Server A lookup/connection delay, completely restart the client to clear the session, and begin again.
